newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian palm olein down on intervention threat.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian palm olein down on intervention threat.

text.p: Indonesia's edible oils market was nervous on Tuesday ahead of a possible government importation of cooking oil to dampen prices, traders said.
"Buyers are taking no new speculative positions ahead of the proposed intervention. They are buying only what they need," one trader said.
They said ready palm olein in Jakarta was lower at 1,570-80 rupiah/kg from Monday's 1,600 rupiah/kg.
"I think with the BULOG intervention and the higher export taxes next month the market has now topped out," one trader said.
Zero export taxes during August created a local shortage of crude palm oil (CPO) and palm olein and higher prices as producers rushed to export as much as possible this month.
The state logisitics agency BULOG said on the weekend it planned to import cooking oil to curb domestic prices when needed. The agency did not mention any quantities.

Industry sources said on Tuesday BULOG could import as much between 20,000 and 30,000 tonnes from Malaysia by early next month, although traders said it was impossible to know what position BULOG would actually take.
The industry sources said if the price did not then fall to the agency's prefered range of 1,400-50 rupiah then another similar amount of palm olein could then be imported.
"A lot of it is psychological," one said. The threat of an intervention itself would be enough to lower prices, he said.
Traders said forward oil was at 1,520-25 rupiah/kg for the end of September.

Crude palm oil (CPO) sold at tender last week at 1,222.5 rupiah/kg in Medan was still firm despite the threat of the intervention. It was seen being traded at between 1,240-80 rupiah/kg at a tender expected later on Tuesday.
